headline: High-risk write/network overlap and output-trust issues in OpenHands; awesome-python is non-runnable but can still be misused as untrusted content.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: OpenHands can read files in its runtime and use MCP/browser/tooling, so if awesome-python content is copied into that workspace or an MCP channel, it may be treated as trusted input. awesome-python itself is non-runnable and has no I/O surfaces, so the bridge is indirect, but the shared-file/manual handoff pathway is plausible.
conditions: IF awesome-python content is manually pasted or mounted into OpenHands runtime files
IF OpenHands parses that content as instructions or tool directives
mitigations: Keep awesome-python content outside the OpenHands workspace
Disable MCP servers for the session
Use a read-only mount for any reference material
Add a human review step before executing file-derived instructions

B_data_leakage.rationale: awesome-python touches no data classes and has no network egress, while OpenHands can read runtime files and has broad egress. The pair does not show a default shared workspace, so leakage is not established by the profiles alone; however, if sensitive files are mounted into OpenHands, they can be transmitted outward.
conditions: IF sensitive files are mounted into the OpenHands runtime
IF OpenHands is allowed to call external APIs or model providers
mitigations: Do not mount sensitive directories into OpenHands
Use a local-only model provider
Restrict outbound network at the container boundary
Rotate any secrets already placed in the runtime

C_capability_conflict.rationale: awesome-python has no write or execution capabilities, but OpenHands can write files, modify git state, and spawn shells. If both are used against the same mounted volume or repo, OpenHands can overwrite or race with artifacts referenced by awesome-python-derived workflows. The conflict is plausible through shared files, though not proven as default.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same mounted repository or volume
IF OpenHands is permitted to modify git state in that workspace
mitigations: Assign separate workspaces per agent
Mount shared inputs read-only
Require git locks or a single-writer policy
Pause OpenHands before any repo mutation

D_cascading_error.rationale: OpenHands can act on files and browser/tool outputs, so if it consumes awesome-python content as authoritative guidance, errors or stale references can cascade into incorrect actions. awesome-python is a curated collection rather than an execution agent, which lowers direct risk, but the lack of verification in the handoff still creates a default failure mode when used as source material.
conditions: IF OpenHands uses awesome-python entries as authoritative instructions
IF no separate verification step checks the referenced package or command
mitigations: Require source verification before acting on any listed item
Treat awesome-python as a directory, not a recommendation
Add a confirmation prompt before shell or browser actions
Log provenance for each derived action

E_compliance.rationale: No PHI, residency, or retention mismatch is documented for awesome-python, and OpenHands only explicitly handles files in its runtime plus model-provider API keys. The profiles do not show a concrete compliance conflict, but if regulated data is mounted into OpenHands, its broad egress and external model calls could create policy issues.
conditions: IF regulated data is mounted into the OpenHands runtime
IF the configured model provider stores prompts or files outside the required jurisdiction
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the runtime
Use a jurisdiction-approved model provider
Review retention settings before launch
Document the data flow for the session
